routes.name: Residency according to the EU/EEA regulations

note: Norway, read on the Directorate of Immigration's own pages (udi.no, read 2026-10-30): skilled workers, fees, EU/EEA residency and permanent residence. A foreigner from outside the EU/EEA who wants to work in Norway needs a residence permit for work; a skilled worker (higher education, vocational training or special qualifications) needs a concrete job offer from one employer in Norway. Where the position needs a degree, the permit is normally up to three years at a time (up to one through a staffing agency); after three years the holder may apply for permanent residence. A change of employer in the same type of position needs no new permit, a new type of position does: the game reads it as work for the sponsor. The fee is NOK 6,300 for an adult's residence permit for work, renewals too; a permanent residence permit costs NOK 4,000 for an adult. The permit for cultural workers and the self-employed did not answer at the addresses tried. Residence permits entitle the holder to work unless the decision says otherwise (the fees page), so the permanent permit is read as any work. EU/EEA nationals have the right to live, work and study in Norway. Citizenship's years and decision times were not read.

sources.title: Skilled workers, UDI (read 2026-10-30)
sources.said: You must have received a concrete job offer from one specific employer in Norway. ... If the position requires that you have completed an education or degree from a university/ university college, you can normally get a residence permit for up to three years at a time. ... After three years, you can apply for a permanent residence permit in Norway. ... If you are later going to change employers, but work in the same type of position, you do not need to apply for a new residence permit.

sources.title: Fees, UDI (read 2026-10-30)
sources.said: Residence permits for work for applicants over the age of 18 (also renewals) ... NOK 6 300 ... Permanent residence permit for adults ... NOK 4 000 ... that entitle the holder to work unless otherwise specified in the decision

sources.title: Residency according to the EU/EEA regulations, UDI (read 2026-10-30)
sources.said: If you are an EU/EEA national you have the right to live, work and study in Norway.
